blind_comparisons.question: Which of these two 900-frame camera height residual series is a camera bolted to a character, and which is a camera bolted to a walk cycle? The tell is a spectral peak at the footfall frequency.
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: Neither is a walk-cycle camera. B's spectrum has a 2.19x peak-over-median at 2.07 Hz, in the plausible footfall band, but its absolute magnitude is 4.6e-08 m — 46 nanometres, i.e. quantisation, not motion. A is bit-exactly zero at all 900 samples with a flat spectrum. Both pass RI-CAM06 §E's stdev and peak bars, and the item's discriminator does not separate them. Secondary identification guess, recorded before reveal: A looked synthetic, because a bit-exact zero residual over 900 samples is what an analytic series produces.

blind_comparisons.question: Which of these two angle(input_direction, character_facing) series for the same scripted 180 degree reversal at run speed is a character with mass? A series that goes 180 -> 0 in one frame is the tell.
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: Neither snaps, so both have mass — but B is the series a rate-limited turn law produces: an exactly linear ramp at 12.0 deg/frame (RI-CAM02 §C's moving cap of 720 deg/s), closing 168 degrees in exactly 14 frames and holding at 0. A ramps at 8.0 deg/frame — §C's stationary cap — and then plateaus at a residual 45 degrees that never closes.

biggest_gap.what: The seeded PRNG is reseeded correctly and never drawn from. rng.draws is 0 on every one of 3600 frames in every scenario, state and seed measured. Seeds 1337 and 4242 over a 3600-frame duel differ in exactly one field — .rng.seed, the echo of the input — and in zero simulation fields (r4-seed-sensitivity.txt: 'frames differing in ANY field other than .rng.seed: 0'). RI-MTH02 R4's 5%-of-frames clause is therefore satisfied at 100% by that echo alone, so the rung, tools/harness/determinism.mjs, and any future critic reading either will report seed sensitivity on a build that has none. The build's own ladder prints 'PASS R4 — seed-sensitive ... frames_differing_pct: 100'.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Every downstream claim of seeded variety — RI-AI01 M4's inter-COMMIT coefficient of variation, rumours that differ per town, seeded loot placement — is unfalsifiable until the seed reaches something, and the corpus's own detector for that condition currently returns PASS.

remedy.action: (1) Route at least one simulation quantity through rng.next() inside the fixed step and emit the draw count truthfully — the enemy idle-loop phase offset chosen at spawn is sufficient, cheap, and is exactly the field AM-W1-00-01 wants excluded from R5, so seeding it converts that argument into a measurement. (2) Change tools/harness/determinism.mjs's R4 computation to drop the rng.seed field before counting differing frames, and to fail the rung with reason 'prng_never_drawn' when max(rng.draws) == 0 in either run. (3) Adopt orchestration/amendments/AM-W1-00-C1-mth02-r4-discriminator.md, which states the sharpened rung and moves no threshold.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run node tools/harness/trace.mjs --scenario cmb-duel-infantry at seeds 1337 and 4242 and diff field-by-field: max(rng.draws) > 0 in both runs, and >= 5% of frames differ in at least one field OTHER than .rng.seed. The second number is currently 0.0% (0 of 3600 frames) and is recorded in r4-seed-sensitivity.txt.

secondary_observations.what: queueInputs silently accepts and no-ops an event with no recognised action key: {f:0,tap:'light'} returns 1, {f:0,wibble:3} returns 1, {f:0} returns 1, and none of them fire. Unknown BUTTONS throw correctly; unknown EVENT SHAPES do not. This cost me four measurements before I noticed — probes 3, 6, 8 and 10 all ran with their attack inputs silently dropped. HARNESS.md §4 does not require the game to accept tap/hold sugar, but returning a count for an event that will never fire is fail-quiet where RI-MTH01 M6 asks for fail-closed.

arbitration_questions.question: AM-W1-00-01 asks to permanently exclude enemies[].anim_frame and enemies[].state_entered_f from RI-MTH02 R5 on the ground that a looping idle makes the rung unsatisfiable. Should it be adopted?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: Adopt it. The arithmetic is correct — (p + 60) mod 48 != p unless the loop length divides the warm-up delta — and a statue between actions would make RI-AI02's readable-telegraph measurements meaningless, so the build cannot fix the rung by deleting the idle loop.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: Do not adopt it as written. It was filed by a build with no enemy AI, rng.draws 0 everywhere, and an enemy state histogram of {FACE: 1800}, so its claim that the two fields are cosmetic is true only under conditions that make it untestable. It also mis-diagnoses its own failure: R5 still fails on arena_flat with NO enemy present, where the sole differing field is events[i].f — a second absolute frame index M5's re-basing instruction does not reach. The correct correction is therefore to re-base the enumerable set of absolute frame indices (f, events[].f, enemies[].state_entered_f), which leaves anim_frame as the only genuinely warm-up-dependent quantity and precisely the one that must not be excluded once animation drives a hurtbox.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-MTH04 §A mandates an `evidence:` block in every verdict, and verdict.schema.json (additionalProperties: false) has no field for it. Which document wins?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: The schema wins: a verdict that does not validate cannot be aggregated, and every field the evidence block needs (path, produced_by, seed, sha256, run command) already exists in artifacts[] and build.harness_commands[].
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: RI-MTH04 wins: it is the anti-fabrication item, its `claims`/`unmeasured` lists have no home in the schema at all, and 'a number in the prose with no claims entry' is one of its four tells. Either the schema gains an `evidence` object or RI-MTH04 must state that artifacts[] plus method_deviations[] discharge it.

notes: AR-3 (seam sterility, ARBITRATION.md §3): seam_sterile = TRUE. This piece carries zero boundary-crossing interactions and I do not think it should carry any — it is the measurement seam itself: a fixed-step loop, a trace format, an input pipeline and a save blob, none of which can make a faction rank change what an enemy does. The justification the rule requires is that W1-00 is the substrate on which every future crossing is measured. But there is one place where it does bear on the seam and there it fails: with rng.draws == 0 and the seed reaching nothing, no future crossing that is supposed to VARY — a rumour that differs by town, an enemy that varies its opening, seeded loot — can be demonstrated to vary at all.
